data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year strengthening of GBP 3.4 million in 2015, primarily driven by adverse claims development across the 2006-2012 years of account. Specifically, GBP 0.4 million related to older years (2006-2010), GBP 2.2 million to the 2011 year of account, and GBP 0.8 million to the 2012 year of account. The 2012 and 2013 years of account were placed into run-off due to ongoing uncertainty, including potential Australian tax rebates and reserving volatility. The 2014 year of account also saw a recalibration of liability loss ratios and significant property losses from CAT events in Australia and the UK, including Storm Desmond.
raw_causal_phrases: on-going uncertainty over the final loss arising from a combination of factors
potential tax rebate of GBP 2.8m, not held on the balance sheet
continuing assessment of the reserving position due to volatility experienced
changes in capital providers between 2012 and 2013
similar uncertainty existing on a potential tax rebate of up to GBP 1.0m and with reserving uncertainties to also consider
move to further strengthen the liability class of business given adverse movement experienced in older years of account

uncertainty surrounds the ultimate claims loss ratios due to the late earning of the risks, particularly the liability book which has the longest tail of the classes of business written and has seen a volatile pattern in preceding years
recalibration of the liability loss ratios to take in to account patterns seen in the adverse development in older years
extension of the core sports and leisure binders
significant property losses which have stemmed from a number of CAT events in Australia and the UK

uncertainty over a possible beneficial factor to be attributed to this year of account. A material Australian coverholder is looking to secure a rebate of Australian non-resident insurer taxes already paid and expensed in the 2013 year of account results to date.
